title: SLO declaration and priority failover matrix for multi-region model endpoints
creator: Liam Ortega
description:
Purpose: Establish a machine-actionable SLO/SLI declaration format and an operator-facing priority failover matrix that governs multi-region routing, circuit-breaker triggers, and load-shedding for model endpoints. Scope: per-endpoint and per-model SLI definitions (latency, success, quality proxy), composite endpoint SLOs, error-budget burn classifications, regional failover tiers, and concrete mitigation actions (rate limits, model demotion, regional ejection).

SLI definitions (per endpoint/model):
- request_success: fraction of requests that produce a non-error generation (status 200 + generation_complete) measured per 5m window. Primary production availability SLI.
- gen_error_rate: fraction of requests returning 5xx, 4xx generation failures, or aborted streams. Measured as rolling 5m and 1h windows for burn-rate.
- latency_p90_ms: 90th percentile server-side generation latency (end-to-end production time, excluding client network) over 5m and 1h windows. Baseline established per model+route.
- latency_p99_ms: 99th percentile tail latency — used for tail-SLO protection.
- quality_anchor_pass_rate: daily regression-check pass rate against a small immutable promptset (anchor set) used for deployment gating and to flag quality-related SLO regressions.

SLO templates (applies to each endpoint-model variant):
- Latency SLO: latency_p90_ms <= baseline_p90 * 1.25 (monthly) and latency_p99_ms <= baseline_p99 * 1.5 (monthly).
- Availability SLO: request_success >= 99.95% (monthly) for Tier-1 critical routes, 99.9% for Tier-2, 99.5% for Tier-3.
- Quality SLO: quality_anchor_pass_rate >= 98% (rolling 7d).

Composite SLOs and weighting: weight availability 0.6, latency 0.3, quality 0.1 for customer-facing generative chat routes. For non-critical embedding-only endpoints: availability 0.8, latency 0.2. We store these weights in the SLO manifest to support automated burn calculations and prioritization decisions.

Error-budget burn policy (machine-actionable):
- Green: burn_rate <= 1x -> normal ops.
- Caution: 1x < burn_rate <= 3x sustained for 15m -> trigger alert, reduce best-effort traffic for Tier-3 routes by 20%, pause non-essential background jobs.
- Severe: 3x < burn_rate <= 10x sustained for 10m -> enable circuit-breaker soft-fallback: demote requests to quantized model variant (if compatible), reduce batch sizes, and begin regional load rebalancing.
- Critical: burn_rate > 10x or sustained Severe for >30m -> automatic regional ejection for overloaded region, global rate limit for unauthenticated/self-serve routes, and engage on-call.
Burn-rate definition: ratio of current error budget consumption rate to allowed burn rate for the SLO window (standard SRE burn-rate approach).

Circuit breaker triggers and actions (per-region, per-service):
- Error-rate trigger: gen_error_rate > 1.5% over 5m for Tier-1 routes OR > 3% for Tier-2 for 2 consecutive 5m windows -> open circuit for new requests from lowest-priority customers for 5 minutes, reroute to fallback region when available.
- Tail-latency trigger: latency_p99_ms exceeds baseline_p99 by > 1500ms for 5m -> partially open circuit and decrease allowed concurrency for affected model by 30%.
- Queue-pressure trigger: pending_requests > 500 or request_queue_time > 2500ms at edge for 2m -> evict Tier-3 and background jobs, refuse new best-effort requests.
- Consequence mapping: each trigger maps to a ranked action list (evict, demote, reroute, rate-limit, ejection). The actions are applied incrementally and reversible when metrics return to safe ranges.

Load-shedding strategy (policy primitives):
1) Priority-aware queue eviction: preserve prefixes/ongoing KV caches for active sessions; evict requests by customer tier (Tier-3 first).
2) Model demotion: transparent fallback to quantized or smaller variant with documented quality delta. Use quality_anchor_pass_rate to decide whether demotion is acceptable.
3) Graceful rejection: return a structured 429 with guidance + retry-after and optional streaming partial response for long-running generation.
4) Token-based throttling: limit tokens/sec per project when token burn is driving cost/latency instability.
5) Soft-degradation: reduce max_tokens and sampling complexity (temperature/top_p adjustments) for non-critical routes to reduce compute footprint.

Multi-region failover matrix (operator-facing):
- Each region assigned: Tier-1 (primary), Tier-2 (preferred failover), Tier-3 (cold backup). Assignment considers latency SLA, data residency, and capacity headroom.
- Failover decision factors (scored): operational health (50%), SLO-compliance signal (20%), capacity headroom (15%), latency delta (10%), data residency compliance (5%). Score thresholds define automatic failover, weighted to bias against cross-border failovers that violate residency.
- Failover policy examples: if primary region health_score < 0.6 AND burn_rate > 3x -> failover to highest-scoring Tier-2 in the same legal domain; if none available, perform partial regional ejection and offload to dedicated reserved capacity (if customer is on Dedicated).

Observability & runbook:
- Dashboards: per-endpoint, per-model SLI panels (p50/p90/p99 latency; error rate; burn-rate heatmap; quality_anchor trend; per-region capacity).
- Alerts: multi-channel SRE alert for Caution/Severe/Critical with runbook links and suggested mitigations. Pager triggers on Critical.
- Playbook steps (short): detect -> validate (confirm via two independent metrics) -> mitigate (apply ranked actions) -> monitor -> escalate -> postmortem.

Decision trade-offs and notes:
- Preserving quality for critical customers vs maximizing availability for free-tier: adopt tiered protections rather than one-size-fits-all.
- Demotion to quantized models reduces cost but may increase hallucinations; require quality_anchor checks before enabling demotion for Tier-1.
- Conservative thresholds to avoid flapping; use smoothing windows and cooldown timers.

- Confluence SLO spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/REGIONAL+SLO+DECLARATION
- GitHub runtime changes (SLO manifest + breaker controller): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482

Acceptance criteria:
- SLO manifest schema checked in and loaded by policy engine.
- Automated burn-rate policy exercises simulated with staged load and produces expected action sequence.
- Runbook validated by SRE tabletop and minor edits captured.

Next steps:
- Resolve open review comments from SRE and PM (see comments).
- Wire SLO manifest into traffic-router decision API and breaker controller.
- Schedule tabletop for 2026-03-20 with on-call rotation.
